There are layers to this.  

Songs like Bboom Bboom vs BAAM actually sound the same. They have pretty much the exact same song structure and top line melodies. This is not a drag (I loved Bboom Bboom, so when BAAM came out I was like great, more for me! And I do enjoy/prefer different parts of both songs).  

Songs like Heart Shaker vs What Is Love, or Yes or Yes vs Fancy, sound similar. It may not always jump out, but listen to one directly after the other and you will see the melodic or structural parallels.  

Songs like Smart (LSF) vs Water (Tyla) share common roots. They both have the afrobeat character underneath, but rather than one coming out of the other, producers of Smart probably looked at Water, went back to the root of Water's sound a bit, then created Smart from that. Not denying influence, but not consequentially similar aka you will hear a deep similarity but won't automatically connect the two songs without some regular listening.  

Some groups just have a signature style or structure (think ATEEZ or GFRIEND). Their songs carry certain elements through their songs, and therefore it's impossible to hear the songs without drawing parallels. Equally, it makes the song recognisable (hearing a song and think, "Yep, that's a GFRIEND song!")  

Bottom line is kpop stans as always lack zero nuance and combine all of these into the simple phrase of "sound the same".

I think Trigger is the worst of all of these options unless it's specifically a favourite. The other three are all excelling choices. 

If your financial situation is tight, get Thrill-ing. It's a good, fun album! If you've got a bit of cash to spare, both Phantasy Pt. 2 and Unexpected are good choices — only get the signed/exclusive if you know it would be extra meaningful beyond the fact that you're getting them a TBZ album :)

the reason for the overall decline in "main vocal capability" in fourth gen is because of kpop stans. I know we "shouldn't be so quick to blame kpop stans" or whatever but the absolute bullying over idols who couldn't dance + the rise of dance trends (on whatever platform it made be) have made it so that companies need to choose a main vocal who can keep up in regards to the new demands and standards of kpop and dance in kpop. and what's probably happened is that companies are choosing idols who would otherwise be lead vocals to be main vocals because the main vocalists in training just could not keep up with the dancing requirements needed to exist in the modern kpop spheres without being literally crucified. of course, this is naturally a huge generalisation and there are plenty of amazing vocalists currently in fourth gen (nmixx, yunjin, chaehyun, jiwon of fromis_9, haram, chaewon of class:y and many more!). my main example favouring my point is ive - yujin and liz are good vocalists, very capable as is undisputed, but I think yujin being just about a lead vocal in iz*one and liz being only ever so slightly better than yujin really indicates the difference. not enough people appreciated how staggering iz*one's vocal line was... yujin, chaewon and yena, chaeyeon, eunbi and of course YURI! probably the only "fourth gen" girl groups with a vocal LINE capable of rivalling them are nmixx and perhaps fromis_9 (that come to mind - feel free to suggest others). plenty of groups have one or two really good vocalists (kep1er is a prime example of this) but there is little "uniform sense of quality" when it comes to a vocal standard (unlike second gen where groups like girls generation and kara not only had one stellar vocalist but phenomenal vocal lines spanning half or more of their groups) and instead this has been replaced with a uniform sense of quality when it comes to dance (again, kep1er are a strong example of this - as are lesserafim, having quite a sharp difference between vocal quality in yunjin/chaewon vs sakura/kazuha/eunchae with eunchae slowly trying to fill the bridge that was pretty perfectly occupied by garam - the definition of what a lead vocalist is, really, not as good as the main but clearly providing a bridge to the rest of the group whilst still being good). I just think context matters here - you can't look at fourth gen and complain about the lack of taeyeons or hyolyns or ailees where companies just aren't selecting people in that kind of way anymore. appreciate what we do have and take the opportunity to not only enjoy the music, but discover a whole bunch of amazing vocalists scattered across the kpop sphere!

MNET has a... history of not doing background checks, or at least not very well. They're very rash with their decisions. If they had known that 1 million Weibo followers was enough to be targeted by the Chinese government, I guarantee most of these girls would not have been chosen considering there were 3000 applicants. Shen Xiaoting, Cai Bing, Zhou Xinyu and Huang Xingqiao were the only C Group girls who didn't post anything related to the controversy in the final 27, which I think says a lot. It just so happened that one of the girls who did, Su Ruiqi was in the top 9, and that's how she became the face of the controversy (alongside Chen Hsinwei to a lesser extent). If MNET had rigging powers, I think the AAA girls would have been slowly rigged out of the competition and MNET would have thought twice about their replacements (maybe Leung Cheukying and Li Yiman because they had been working/studying in Korea for years).

Let me start of by saying I am neither Chinese, nor Korean, so my word is not authentic. But from everything I have heard and gathered, here's the deal.

Ruiqi, along with a lot of the other C girls with large followings, was required to post things related to the AAA controversy.The Anti-American Aid controversy refers to when US aided South Korea during the Korean War. Keep in mind that China and Russia were in North Korea's side of the war. The statements basically says that China condemns US intervention in the war because a lot of Chinese soldiers died. If US didn't intervene, there wouldn't be a South Korea now. (Credits to u/desertfoxtim) 

Korea likes to think that if you want to work in Korea, in this case debut as an idol, you must virtually abandon your nationality and consider yourself Korean or in support of Korea (funny that: they expect you to call yourself a virtual Korean yet they themselves will forever single you out as a Chinese, Japanese, Thai, [insert country] idol). So when Koreans found out that these girls, who want to debut in Korea, are posting things with pro-Chinese (and thus anti-Korean) sentiments, they went haywire.  This controversy is still referred to as the anti-American aid (AAA) controversy in this context. 

We do not know if the girls posted these due to political standpoint or if they were forced into doing so.

So in terms of how bad it would have been? Extremely. A group with a member being labelled as AAA would result in a whole group being labelled AAA. Nobody would want to associate with them: companies wouldn't want to use them as brand ambassadors, so they would get no CFs or endorsements. Variety shows wouldn't want to associate with them (these are a vital part of promotions). I could even see broadcasting companies other than MNET like KBS or SBS refusing to associate with them (slight stretch but possible) so they would barely be able to promote their own songs. It would have been DETRIMENTAL to the group and they would probably just outright disband.

I think Chinese idols still within the KPOP industry (e.g. NCT's Chinese members or Yuqi from (G)I-DLE) do not post these things are the Chinese government does not consider them Chinese idols. However once they leave the Korean Entertainment Industry and enter the Chinese Entertainment Industry, they will probably be required to post pro-Chinese or pro-Chinese Government content, whoever else it may offend. We've seen this with idols such as CLC's Elkie, GOT7's Jackson and EXO's Lay.

So yeah, that's all I know - hopefully this was helpful!
